items.title: Passing the Cup of Sorrows
items.note: A return to solo piano for the Disintegration Loops composer, recorded alone and mostly unadorned. Spare and meditative, with more grief in it than usual.

items.title: FUDGE
items.note: His first album since going public with a serious health battle, and it sounds like a man taking his time to get things right. Warm, classic soul songwriting, understated rather than showy.

items.title: Heaven Can Wait
items.note: Her first release on Ghostly International, a euphoric, slightly woozy track about the rush of city life. Short and good, worth the three minutes.

items.title: Sing the Color Blue
items.note: Chicago drummer Mike Reed's genre-blurring quintet, moving between post-bop, chamber music and something closer to indie rock without ever losing the swing.

items.title: Aldehydes and Ketones
items.note: His first solo single in almost five years, slow burning with a heavy low end and textures that feel like they're dissolving as you listen. Genuinely strange in a good way.

items.title: LP1
items.note: Ex GoGo Penguin drummer Rob Turner and keyboardist Liviu Gheorghe's debut as a duo, spiritual jazz run through beat driven electronics. Good for anyone who liked GoGo Penguin but wanted it rougher round the edges.

items.title: theukhasmorefoodbanksthanbranchesofmcdonalds.com
items.note: Built entirely from samples of food bank items, pasta, tinned fruit, toilet roll, as a pointed piece about poverty in Britain. Conceptual in a way that could feel gimmicky but mostly just lands.

items.title: We Never Learn (feat. Kudbeu)
items.note: A restrained, quietly ecstatic deep house cut from one of South Africa's steadiest producers. Good late night driving music.

items.title: It's a Style Sport
items.note: Ishmael Butler's project keeps mutating, this one woozier and more collaged than the last couple of records. Dense and slippery, rewards repeat listens.

items.title: Edge Conditions
items.note: Modular synths woven through acoustic instruments and field recordings into something warm and human, a little Jon Hassell in its spirit. Came out a couple weeks back but too good to leave off.
